item.title: Messi receives top Spanish award from heir to throne
item.description: Lionel Messi received Spain’s most prestigious sports award on Friday in recognition of his glittering career and his work for disadvantaged children’s access to health and education. The Argentine forward, 39, was named winner of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports in June, with the jury hailing “the most successful footballer of all time” and his social work. Dozens of fans wearing Argentina football shirts cheered and chanted Messi’s name as he arrived to the sound of bagpipes and drums at the ceremony in Oviedo, capital of the northern Spanish region of Asturias. Messi collected a formal roll of parchment from Princess Leonor, the heir to the Spanish throne after whom the awards are named, who lauded his “unique career”. “He turned the extraordinary into routine by reading the game and deciding on the most effective option in fractions of a second, while respecting the collective essence above ego,” Leonor said. One of the greatest footballers of all time, Messi has won eight Ballon d’Or titles, a World Cup and dozens of trophies at club level. He spent 21 years at Barcelona where he played in a side that dominated Spain and Europe under Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique. After leaving the Catalan club in 2021, Messi spent two years at French giants Paris Saint-Germain and currently plays for Inter Miami in MLS. Argentina’s all-time top goalscorer, assist provider and caps holder called time on his international career earlier this year after losing the World Cup final to Spain in New Jersey. “The most important thing is to know how to lose and how to win,” Messi told an event with children in Oviedo on Thursday, saying that attitude was “fundamental” in football. Founded in 1981, the Princess of Asturias Awards are the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world and come with prize money of 50,000 euros ($56,000). They encompass the arts, sciences and sports and are handed out annually in honour of efforts to improve human coexistence, solidarity and global cooperation. British author Julian Barnes, trailblazing US astronaut Christina Koch and punk star Patti Smith were among the other winners who received their prize on Friday. Previous winners of the sports award include tennis greats Serena Williams and Rafael Nadal, marathon record-breaker Eliud Kipchoge and US skier Lindsey Vonn. item.title: BBNaija should take a break, re-strategise— Tacha
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Reality TV star Natacha Akide has urged Big Brother Naija organisers to take a break and re-strategise, saying the show needs fresh ideas to hold viewers’ attention in an entertainment landscape increasingly shaped by social media. Speaking on Arise 360 on Arise News, the former housemate said the show’s earlier success came at a time when social media played a different role in people’s lives. “I think they need to take a break, restrategise and just come up with something because we are really at an era where everything happens on social media,” she said. Tacha argued that online conversations now compete with reality television for viewers’ attention, pointing to the ongoing public interest in the dispute involving music duo P-Square. “You don’t want us watching housemates in the house, meanwhile P-Square is giving us part seven of his family issues… we have come to a point where everyone is so comfortable with social media right now,” she said. She suggested that stepping away for a while could give audiences time to miss the programme before it returns with a refreshed format. “You also give Nigerians a chance to miss you,” she said. Tacha called on the organisers to develop concepts that would feel new and more compelling to Nigerian viewers. “They need to cook, like they need to try to do something different which will be much more mind-blowing and more interesting to Nigerians because Nigerians are hard to please,” she added Tacha rose to prominence on the 2019 “Pepper Dem” edition of BBNaija, but was disqualified following a physical altercation with fellow housemate Mercy Eke. Since leaving the show, she has pursued ventures in entertainment and fashion, worked as a radio host on 96.9 Cool Fm and launched Tacha FC in 2024. item.title: Russia says Ukraine, US talks ‘planned’ for Abu Dhabi
item.description: Talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday. Russia indicated its readiness to resume the talks, which have been at a standstill since the beginning of the year, following a meeting this week in Saint Petersburg between President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff. The next round of talks towards ending the Ukraine war, which is grinding through its fifth year, are “planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi”, and “will take place in a trilateral format”, Peskov told reporters. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the plan to meet in November in a post on X. “Now we all need to focus on making these meetings happen –- together with America, Europe, and all our partners,” he said Friday. The announcement came amid intensified diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump’s administration. Witkoff met on Tuesday with Zelensky and European leaders in Oslo, before meeting with Putin on Wednesday. Following the meetings, both Kyiv and Moscow voiced their readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington. Russia, which launched its full-scale offensive against Ukraine in February 2022, has suggested talks could take place “around November 10”. Zelensky has called for the discussions to happen “as soon as possible”. In a televised interview aired late Thursday, Putin said that any trilateral talks would focus on the security arrangements of a final peace deal and not a “short” truce. item.title: Coastal Road: ‘I’m local champion; you’re pretender’ — Gov Diri replies Duke
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has hit back at former Cross River State governor and Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate Donald Duke, calling him a “jester and a pretender” after Duke’s remarks about the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. In a recent interview on Arise Television, the PRP candidate called governor Diri a “local champion” while arguing that the coastal road project was not feasible because of its cost and Bayelsa State’s terrain. Diri had earlier rejected Duke’s claim that building the highway through Bayelsa was not feasible, adding that the ex-governor is “not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure” in Bayelsa. Reacting to Diri’s comment, Duke said: “The governor of Bayelsa, if he did say so, I don’t know the fellow, but if he did say so, I think he’s just being a local champion.” One week after Duke’s comment, Governor Diri, in a video which has now gone viral, fired back at the PRP candidate, saying he’s a local champion elected to defend his people. “Yes, I’m a local champion, because that is where I was raised. I am elected to defend the local people. I am elected to champion their cause. But Donald Duke, let me ask you, you were on seat when Bakassi was ceeded out of Nigeria. “You were the sitting governor of Cross River state. Because you are not a local champion, you did nothing about it. I believe that you are more of a jester and a pretender,” he said. Diri also questioned Duke’s political standing in his own ward, and said the dispute was about his people and the region, not simply a personal disagreement. “Donald Duke, I am not one who takes up people, I am not one of those who insult people; I don’t insult leaders; I don’t insult elders but what you have done is not just about me, it is about my environment, it is about my people.” The governor further defended the region’s development potential, saying Bayelsa and other coastal communities should not be defined by their difficult terrain. “Donald Duke, I am not that fellow, I am the sitting governor of Bayelsa state. All of us from this region, particularly from Bayelsa state, do not accept the narrative that your state cannot be developed. We have a very rich ancestry, our terrain is one of the best if we develop it and we are prepared to take our destiny into our hands.” Diri also thanked the President for supporting the coastal road, describing it as an opportunity to address poverty and the dehumanisation of coastal communities. item.title: U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat North Korea 3-1 to reach knockout stage
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s Flamingos have advanced to the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match. The Flamingos secured the victory at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco on Friday. Nigeria went into the encounter needing a win to guarantee their progress after losing to Poland in their second match, having opened their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico. Akeem Busari’s side rose to the occasion, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi opening the scoring in the 15th minute. Oluebube Umejiaku extended Nigeria’s lead in the 38th minute, beating North Korea’s high defensive line before finishing past the goalkeeper. Kanyisola Yusuf then put the Flamingos firmly in control with a third goal early in 56th minutes North Korea pulled one back through a penalty in the 82nd minutes, but Nigeria held firm defensively to preserve their two-goal advantage and secure the victory. The result saw Nigeria finish second in Group B behind North Korea, who claimed top spot on goals scored. Poland ended the group stage in third place despite finishing level on points with the top two teams. item.title: US could strike Iran this weekend, envoy says
item.description: The United States could strike Iran as soon as this weekend, a US envoy said Friday, after mounting threats by both Washington and Israel. “Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and point man on Syria who does not have a direct role on Iran, told podcast host Mario Nawfal. President Donald Trump “is very clear. He’s open and available and accessible to a deal and we’ve been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said in an interview as he visited the Gulf. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces elections Tuesday, has in recent days repeatedly vowed to topple the clerical state in Iran, following two major bombing campaigns against it since last year. Trump has also signalled an openness to resuming strikes after a long deadlock in diplomacy, although he earlier said it would not happen before US congressional elections on November 3. Barrack, in remarks that contradict Netanyahu, said the US was not looking to topple the Islamic republic, a sworn enemy of the United States and Israel since a 1979 revolution toppled the pro-Western shah. “If you keep threatening the world, our allies, the Gulf, there will be a consequence. The consequence won’t be regime change,” Barrack said. “The United States — the president of the United States — has said he’s not interested in regime change,” he added. “The problem with regime change always is, what’s the day-two scenario?” The post US could strike Iran this weekend, envoy says appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: A gunman firing from his car killed one person and wounded five — including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times — in the Paris suburbs Friday, in what the French presidency condemned as a “racist terrorist attack”. French President Emmanuel Macron visited the working-class town of Trappes southwest of Paris, where a gunman opened fire earlier in the day in an attack suspected of having targeted people of foreign origin. This was a “racist, terrorist attack”, said the Elysee presidential palace. Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh said the man was “firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath” as he drove through Trappes and neighbouring La Verriere. Most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds and prosecutors are investigating whether the acts targeted the “real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion” of the victims. The 12-year-old girl shot eight times was “seriously wounded” but in a stable condition, the mayor of La Verriere, Nicolas Dainville, told AFP. Police arrested the alleged shooter — a 39-year-old man, according to a source familiar with the case — in nearby Coignieres. Officers found him in possession of a submachine gun and tear-gas grenades, according to a police source. He had also booby-trapped his flat with three gas canisters and electric wires “connected to a timer”, according to anti-terrorism prosecutors. item.title: Gombe Assembly approves state police
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe The Gombe State House of Assembly has approved proposed constitutional amendments to pave the way for the establishment of State Police in Nigeria. The development followed an earlier statement made to newsmen by the Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriation, Aliyu Baba Manu, that the bill had not been officially presented to lawmakers. According to a report of the Assembly’s proceedings, the lawmakers considered and adopted the recommendations of a seven-member ad hoc committee on constitutional review, endorsing proposed amendments to various provisions of the 1999 Constitution, including those relating to the establishment and operation of State Police Services. With this, 25 state legislatures have endorsed state police The reported action marks a significant step in Gombe State’s participation in the ongoing constitutional process aimed at decentralising policing and strengthening Nigeria’s response to mounting security challenges. The proposed constitutional alteration, reportedly containing 26 clauses, was said to have been transmitted to the state legislature by the National Assembly on October 6, 2026, for consideration in line with Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The proposed reform seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services alongside the Nigeria Police Force, which currently operates under federal control. As part of the process, the Gombe Assembly constituted a seven-member ad hoc committee on constitutional review, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Hon. Sadam Bello Sale, to examine the proposed amendments and make recommendations to the House. Presenting the committee’s report, Sale said members had consulted relevant stakeholders as part of their assignment. He added that the report received the support of a two-thirds majority of lawmakers, in accordance with Order 17, Rule 3 of the Gombe State House of Assembly Standing Orders, 2020. During plenary on Thursday, the lawmakers reportedly considered the committee’s recommendations at the Committee of the Whole and adopted the report, endorsing the proposed amendments, including those concerning State Police Services. item.title: Ronaldo scores 982nd career goal as Al Nassr beat Al Faisaly 3-1
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 982nd official career goal as Al Nassr defeated Al Faisaly 3-1 in the Saudi Pro League on Friday, moving the Portugal captain 18 goals away from reaching the historic 1,000-goal milestone. The 41-year-old forward struck in the 49th minute, heading home a delivery from compatriot João Félix to double Al Nassr’s advantage at Majmaah Sports City Stadium. Ronaldo’s latest goal ended a spell without scoring since his effort against Neftchi Fargona in the AFC Champions League Elite on October 12, bringing his tally for club and country to 982. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner thought he had scored again shortly afterwards, but the effort was ruled out for offside following a review. Abdullah Al-Hamdan opened the scoring for Al Nassr early in the first half, finishing a move involving Sadio Mané to give the visitors the lead. Al Faisaly reduced the deficit through Theo Bongonda, who headed home Mohammed Al Shanqiti’s cross, but Al Nassr restored their two-goal cushion when Ângelo Gabriel scored in the 79th minute after being set up by Al-Hamdan. The victory was Al Nassr’s third consecutive win, following victories over Al-Diriyah and Neom, and kept them firmly in the Saudi Pro League title race. Al Nassr moved to 25 points, level with leaders Al-Qadsiah, who had a game in hand ahead of their fixture against Al-Hilal. Al-Hilal are third, one point behind the leading pair, with a postponed match still to play. item.title: Delta govt approves N4bn to empower 1500 indigenes
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha The Delta State Government has approved N4 billion to empower 15,000 indigent residents to support small businesses and entrepreneurship. The initiative is part of efforts to ease economic hardship across the state. The State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori at Government House, Asaba. The Commissioner who was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Sir Festus Ahon, said beneficiaries will be drawn from the 25 local government areas under an initiative designed to improve livelihoods and strengthen the purchasing power of vulnerable residents. Aniagwu said the intervention would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that the selection process be guided by clear eligibility criteria. According to him, priority will be given to indigent persons who already operate small businesses, those seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable residents who require financial support to improve their circumstances. He said the grant was intended to help existing businesses overcome economic challenges, provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs and enable beneficiaries to meet pressing needs. The commissioner explained that the initiative was part of the government’s efforts to ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans. item.title: Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has reportedly been taken to hospital after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday, amid concerns over a viral infection that has affected his health in recent days. According to Sky Sports Germany, the 40-year-old Belgian received medical attention before being taken by ambulance to a hospital in Munich. A rescue helicopter was also seen landing at Bayern’s training complex at Säbener Straße. Reports said Kompany had been battling a viral infection that caused significant discomfort, including problems with his legs and difficulties climbing stairs. German newspaper Bild also reported that the illness had aggravated problems involving old scar tissue. The former Manchester City captain had experienced health concerns before Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga victory over RB Leipzig last weekend, when he reportedly spent periods of the match seated in the dugout. He subsequently missed training and the pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Champions League meeting with Arsenal on Wednesday, leaving assistant coach Aaron Danks to address the media. Danks said Kompany had been advised to rest while recovering, although he acknowledged that persuading the manager to take time away from his duties was difficult. “Getting Vince to rest is a challenge,” Danks said. Kompany recovered sufficiently to take charge of Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. After the match, he admitted that he had continued working despite the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body,” he said. The latest reports said Kompany was in a stable condition, although the precise circumstances surrounding the reported collapse remained unclear. Bayern had not issued a detailed official medical update at the time of reporting. The German champions are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday, with Kompany’s availability for the fixture uncertain. Assistant coach Danks could take charge if the Belgian requires further time to recover. The post Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

Shaibu recalled the December 3, 2023, military drone strike on civilians attending a Maulud celebration in Tudun Biri, in which at least 85 people were killed, and criticised Tinubu for not personally visiting the community after the tragedy. item.title: Eko Power assures solar users of no penalties
item.description: Eko Power Ltd. says customers who invest in solar energy will not be penalised or disconnected for low electricity consumption. Mr Abiola Aloba, General Manager, Corporate Communication Unit of Eko Power, said this in a statement on Friday in Lagos. The company’s clarification followed a complaint by Mr Raphael Awoseyin on Oct. 19, alleging repeated visits by its personnel after installing an 18-kilowatt solar power system at his property. Awoseyin said that the personnel inspected his prepaid meter over suspicions of meter bypass because it was recording little or no electricity consumption. He also alleged that the company issued him a disconnection notice and demanded N112,606 as a loss-of-revenue charge. Aloba, however, said that the company had cancelled the charge in full and withdrawn the disconnection notice, adding that Awoseyin had never been disconnected. “The ‘Loss of Revenue’ demand has been cancelled in full. It should not have been made, and the customer doesn’t owe us,” he said. Aloba said Eko Power supported customers investing in alternative energy sources and would not penalise them for reducing their dependence on the national grid. “Eko Power supports customers who invest in solar. Low electricity consumption is not a reason to disconnect anyone,” he said. He explained that the customer’s prepaid meter, which had been in service for many years, was found to be faulty during testing. According to him, the company replaced the meter at no cost to the customer and would not impose back-billing, reconciliation charges or other costs arising from the incident. Awoseyin said that he relied mainly on solar energy during the day and used electricity supplied by Eko Power as backup at night. He explained that he briefly switched to the company’s electricity supply to demonstrate that his meter could record consumption. item.title: 2027: NDC guber candidate pledges to industrialise Delta
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Governorship Candidate Mr Chris Iyovwaye, has pledged to drive industrialisation as vehicle for job creation and sustainable development in the state if elected in 2027. Iyovwaye made the pledge during a consultation with Chief Emmanuel Nwachukwu, Managing Director, Benco Pools, and his grassroots movement on Friday in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area of Delta. The NDC delegation, led by Iyovwaye, includes the party’s Delta North senatorial candidate, Mr Victor Ochei, and other candidates from Ika Federal Constituency. Others were the party’s candidates for Ika North-East Constituency I, Mr Sylvester Chukwuedo, and Ika South Constituency, Mrs Ogor Tony-Obuh. Iyovwaye criticised poor management of Delta’s common patrimony and the lack of innovative leadership capable of translating resources into tangible benefits. He said industrialisation would drive economic growth, create employment and promote sustainable development if supported by practical policies and measurable results. The governorship candidate said the NDC remained committed to changing the state’s development trajectory through policies that would unlock its economic potentials. Iyovwaye also expressed confidence in the quality of the party’s candidates across all levels, including its presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. He called for the support of Nwachukwu and his associates, saying Delta has greater economic potential than the reflected current level of development. Also, Ochei thanked Nwachukwu for receiving the delegation and recalled his earlier visit to the business leader a few days before the consultation. He described the developing relationship as a partnership with the potential to benefit all parties, particularly the people. The other candidates outlined their commitment to effective representation and development and reinforced the delegation’s message of coordinated engagement across Ika Federal Constituency and Delta North. The party’s Delta North Senatorial Chairman, Mr Aaron Ebenuwa, also led members of the party leadership on the visit. item.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. item.description: The Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, has met the threshold of two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly as required by law, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill said on Friday. Chairman of the group and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed in a statement that the bill has been approved by 24 Houses of Assembly. “The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill notes with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states,” it said. “The Working Group commends the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.” Members of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill: (L-R) Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Gbajabiamila; Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, addressing journalists on August 3, 2026. (Photo by Lanre Lasisi/Channels TV) It said that in line with Section 9 of the Constitution, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The approval is expected to give constitutional backing to the policing framework that the working group’s draft National Policing Bill, 2026 is designed to implement.
